2. Exploratory Data Analysis
Empirical load profiles across diurnal cycles, weekly patterns, seasonal shifts, and weather dependencies

Key EDA findings confirm that electricity demand in Delhi exhibits a pronounced diurnal swing (averaging 1,278 MW between 04:00 and 15:00), a ~51% seasonal surge from February (3,219 MW) to June (4,858 MW). Temperature showed a moderate positive association with electricity demand, while demand also varied across seasons.

Model Performance Context
The results reflect experimental benchmarks on the chronological 2024 test period. Neither model is universally superior across all operational regimes: Random Forest achieves slightly lower error during standard operational loads (75% of hours), while Linear Regression showed smaller errors when capturing the highest observed test-period peak.

Peak Demand Model Error Context
Random Forest substantially underpredicted the highest observed test-period demand (8,631.53 MW at 2024-06-19 15:05:00), predicting 7,677.32 MW with an error of -954.21 MW (-11.05%). Random Forest showed larger errors for extreme demand observations in this experiment. For the same observation, Linear Regression predicted 8,560.41 MW with an error of -71.12 MW (-0.82%).
6. Model-Based Scenario Projection Module
Demonstration of transparent scenario simulation conditioned upon user-specified exogenous inputs
SCENARIO SIMULATION
MODEL-BASED SCENARIO PROJECTION — NOT AN OBSERVED VALUE
This section displays mathematical simulations generated by the projection module under hypothetical user-defined inputs. It does NOT constitute an actual weather forecast or an observed grid dispatch record. All inputs fall within Delhi's historical physical bounds (temperature: 42.0 to 43.8 °C vs. observed historical max of 46.4 °C).
